hints: The plane is inclined at $\theta$ with $\sin\theta = \frac{7}{25}$ (so $\cos\theta = \frac{24}{25}$).
The force $P$ acts horizontally into the incline.
Resolve forces perpendicular to the plane: $R = 1.2g\cos\theta + P\sin\theta = 1.2(10)\left(\frac{24}{25}\right) + P\left(\frac{7}{25}\right)$.
For the least possible value of $P$, the particle is on the verge of sliding DOWN the plane, so friction $F = \mu R = 0.15R$ acts UP the plane.
Resolve forces parallel to the plane: $F + P\cos\theta = 1.2g\sin\theta$, substitute $F = 0.15R$, and solve for $P$.
walkthrough:
Determine the trigonometric values for the incline:
$$\sin\theta = \frac{7}{25} \implies \cos\theta = \sqrt{1 - \left(\frac{7}{25}\right)^2} = \frac{24}{25}$$

Resolve forces perpendicular to the incline in equilibrium:
$$R = 1.2g\cos\theta + P\sin\theta = 12\left(\frac{24}{25}\right) + P\left(\frac{7}{25}\right) = 11.52 + 0.28P$$

For least P, particle is on the point of sliding down, so limiting friction acts up the plane:
$$F + P\cos\theta = 1.2g\sin\theta$$
$$0.15R + P\left(\frac{24}{25}\right) = 12\left(\frac{7}{25}\right)$$
$$0.15(11.52 + 0.28P) + 0.96P = 3.36$$
$$1.728 + 0.042P + 0.96P = 3.36$$
$$1.002P = 3.36 - 1.728 = 1.632$$
$$P = \frac{1.632}{1.002} = \frac{272}{167} \approx 1.63\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Let us carefully analyze all forces acting on the particle of mass $m = 1.2\text{ kg}$ on the rough inclined plane:
The inclination angle satisfies $\sin\theta = \frac{7}{25}$. By Pythagoras, $\cos\theta = \frac{24}{25}$.
1. Weight of the particle: $W = mg = 1.2 \times 10 = 12\text{ N}$ vertically downwards.
2. Normal reaction $R$ perpendicular to the plane upwards.
3. Horizontal applied force $P\text{ N}$ pushing into the slope.
4. Friction force $F$ along the slope, where at the point of slipping $F = \mu R = 0.15R$.
Step 1: Resolve forces perpendicular to the incline.
The component of weight perpendicular to the slope is $W\cos\theta = 12\left(\frac{24}{25}\right)$.
The horizontal force $P$ pushes into the slope, having a component $P\sin\theta$ perpendicular into the plane:

In equilibrium perpendicular to the slope:
$$R = 12\cos\theta + P\sin\theta$$
$$R = 12\left(\frac{24}{25}\right) + P\left(\frac{7}{25}\right) = 11.52 + 0.28P$$
Step 2: Resolve forces parallel to the incline for the least value of $P$.

For the minimum force $P$ required to prevent the particle from slipping down, the particle is on the verge of sliding down the slope. Therefore, the limiting friction force $F$ acts UP the slope:
$$F + P\cos\theta = W\sin\theta$$
$$0.15R + P\left(\frac{24}{25}\right) = 12\left(\frac{7}{25}\right)$$
Thus, the least possible value of $P$ is $1.63\text{ N}$.
